alert_name: Windows Brute Force — Excessive Failed Logons (4625)
description: Detects an abnormal number of Windows EventID 4625 (failed logon) events from a single source IP within a short time window, indicating a likely automated brute force or password spray attempt against Windows authentication services (SMB, RDP, NTLM).

variants.name: Password Guessing
variants.description: High failure rate from one source IP against one target account.
variants.threshold: More than 10 EventID=4625 events from the same SourceIP targeting the same TargetUser within 5 minutes.

variants.name: Password Spray
variants.description: Low-and-slow failures from one source IP spread across many distinct accounts.
variants.threshold: 5 or more distinct TargetUsers failed against from the same SourceIP within 30 minutes, with no more than 3 failures per individual account.

required_fields.description: Windows Security log event for failed logon.
Source IP address of the authentication request. Must be present and non-null; local system logons (127.0.0.1 or ::1) are excluded.
Account name being authenticated. Exclude machine accounts (names ending in $).
Event timestamp used to calculate the sliding time window.
Integer logon type. Focus on 3 (Network) and 10 (RemoteInteractive/RDP). Exclude 5 (Service) and 4 (Batch) to reduce scheduled-task false positives.
Hex failure reason code. 0xC000006A (wrong password) and 0xC0000064 (bad username) are most relevant.

enrichment_steps: Resolve SourceIP to hostname and check against known-asset inventory.
Check SourceIP against threat intel feeds for prior malicious activity.
Determine if TargetUser account is privileged (admin, service, domain admin).
Look for a subsequent EventID=4624 (successful logon) from the same SourceIP — confirms compromise.
Review LogonType to identify attacked service (3=SMB, 10=RDP).

recommended_actions.detail: Add SourceIP to perimeter firewall deny list or EDR network isolation policy. Confirm with threat intel before blocking shared egress IPs (NAT, VPN).
Review recent logon history for targeted accounts. Check for EventID=4624 success from the same SourceIP. If compromised, disable account and initiate password reset.
Verify lockout threshold is configured and appropriate. Typical recommendation: lock after 10 failures, reset counter after 15 minutes.
Confirm whether RDP (3389) or SMB (445) are exposed to untrusted networks. Restrict to VPN-only or internal segments if not already done.
If EventID=4624 follows the burst of 4625s from the same SourceIP, escalate immediately to Tier 2 / Incident Response and begin containment.

false_positive_notes: Common benign triggers: cached credentials after a password rotation, scheduled tasks with outdated credentials (use LogonType filter to exclude 4 and 5), helpdesk bulk account testing, VPN gateway retries. See detection.md for full false positive guidance.
